name: Make guardian verifier redemption durable and recoverable
description: Guardian-attachment initiation redeems a single-use verifier handle and signs its authority token only in memory, so response loss can strand the ceremony and repeated or concurrent requests lack a durable local single-use boundary.
acceptanceCriteria: Root cause: initiateGuardianAuthorityVerification calls the external verifier and signs a token without any durable consumed-handle or issued-authority record. Behavioral variants: (1) ordinary success, (2) local commit then response loss followed by exact retry, (3) concurrent duplicate redemption, (4) same handle with a mutated adult/learner/org/policy tuple, (5) provider success followed by local persistence failure. Done when successful redemption durably and atomically records a non-secret handle identity, consumed state, and bound authority identity before responding; an exact retry recovers the original still-valid authority; concurrent and mutated retries fail closed; persistence failure returns no authority; attachment validates the durable redemption; raw verifier evidence, bearer tokens, and signing secrets are not retained. A named red-green regression test must fail without the fix and pass with it, with API/integration coverage for all five variants including two-connection contention. Scope is the guardian-attachment redemption boundary and its minimum schema/API/mobile recovery contract; no verifier-vendor selection or unrelated consent-flow redesign. Dependency: WI-2533 consumes this prerequisite; WI-2037 supplies the governing ADR/spec contract. Verification: targeted schema, API service/route, integration, migration, typecheck, and lint suites are strict green.
riskImpact: P1 authorization-integrity risk: non-durable redemption can make a legally required ceremony unrecoverable after response loss and cannot locally enforce single-use or mutated/concurrent replay semantics. A faulty fix could mint duplicate authority or retain sensitive verifier material.
